source: due2-native: a policy is its own data space (decisions/0050, #152)
notes: Authored for due2; no origin result. Two policies by different parties, one corpus (conformance/README.md). ex:partner states two hierarchy edges, ex:copy odrl:includedIn odrl:use and ex:alice odrl:partOf ex:team. Under the union that decisions/0050 replaces, both reached ex:offer's rules, and scenarios 2 and 3 were Permit: the two runs of decisions/0050 § Question, on clingo-i at 0928921. An edge that a policy states is local to it, so each edge widens only ex:partner's own permission (scenario 1). Membership that both policies should see is world data, recorded in the SOTW (scenario 4). Each of scenarios 2 and 3 gives ex:offer alone the same answer, which is law L11 (due2-workflows.md §8). The two policies agree on ex:team, the one node they share (due2-workflows.md §4, Several policies are one corpus).

scenarios.name: the partner's own edges widen its own permission

expected.why: In ex:partner's data space, ex:copy is included in odrl:use and ex:alice is part of ex:team, so every part of ex:teamUseA is T (due2-workflows.md §5.2): Permit.

scenarios.name: the partner's action edge does not reach the offer

expected.why: ex:useB's entry in ex:offer reads ex:offer's closure and the SOTW's, which hold no odrl:includedIn edge from ex:copy, so its action part is F (due2-workflows.md §3.3, §5.2). ex:teamUseA's target part is F: NotApplicable.

scenarios.name: the partner's membership edge does not reach the offer

expected.why: ex:teamUseC's entry in ex:offer reads no odrl:partOf edge from ex:alice to ex:team, since only ex:partner states one, so its party part is F (due2-workflows.md §3.3, §5.2). ex:teamUseA's target part is F: NotApplicable.

scenarios.name: membership recorded in the world reaches both policies

expected.why: The SOTW's closure is in every policy's data space (due2-workflows.md §3.3), so ex:alice is part of ex:team for ex:teamUseC's entry in ex:offer too, and every part of it is T: Permit.
